ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) under s 19 of the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Identity Verification Code of Practice 2011; mandatory screening against the UN Consolidated List (Security Council Resolutions), the New Zealand Sanctions Register administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Russia Sanctions Act 2022 designations, and NZ Police FIU lists; global best-practice screening against OFAC SDN and EU Consolidated lists is required for all MFO client onboarding; ongoing transaction monitoring under FMA AML/CFT supervision; independent audit and annual compliance report under Part 4 of the AML/CFT Act 2009; enhanced continuous monitoring required for a High_Risk_Special_License Multi-Family Office executing Custody_Wire and Swift_Interbank payment rails

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register operated by the Companies Office (MBIE) at www.companiesoffice.govt.nz; business.govt.nz application portal; NZBN (New Zealand Business Number) allocation through the same platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory naming language is English; te reo Maori names are accepted without prohibition if not otherwise restricted; the register operates exclusively in Latin script, therefore any non-Latin-script brand must be rendered in Latin-script transliteration for registration purposes; names must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing NZ registered name, reserved name, or registered business number (s 22 Companies Act 1993 and Name Approval Guidelines issued by the Registrar of Companies)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Rejection is issued by the NZ Companies Office citing the offending limb of s 22 of the Companies Act 1993. Stage 1 - reconsideration: within 10 working days the applicant or registered agent submits a written reconsideration request to the Companies Office Name Approval team attaching trademark registry searches, consent documents from the objecting entity, and comparative evidence of distinctiveness. Stage 2 - alternative name: if reconsideration is declined, an amended name with qualifying or distinguishing suffixes (e.g., '(International)', '(NZ)', '(MFO)', 'Holdings', 'Capital') may be resubmitted through the online Name Search tool. Stage 3 - judicial review: under s 22(8) of the Companies Act 1993 the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for review of an unreasonable refusal, within 20 working days of the final refusal. Extension of a reserved name is not automatic; a new reservation application must be lodged, unless the Companies Office grants an administrative extension in the case of MFO licensing-related delay

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partial - strictly not permissible as the sole registered office. Section 192 of the Companies Act 1993 requires a physical street address in New Zealand open for service of process during business hours; a PO Box or purely virtual address is invalid. Serviced offices, licensed corporate service providers, and registered agent physical offices in Auckland, Wellington, or Christchurch are acceptable. As a Multi-Family Office (MFO) classified as High_Risk_Special_License under the AML/CFT and FMC Act regimes, the entity must additionally maintain in-country premises or a demonstrable agent with local custody of CDD/AML records, discretionary investment management protocols, and Swift interbank/trust administration documentation
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated_Moderate (annualized likelihood of approximately 30-35%); unannounced physical inspections under s 130 of the AML/CFT Act 2009 and FMA monitoring powers arise most frequently in the first 12 months of licensing where discretionary portfolio advisory services are provided to multiple private client families; desk-based reviews occur near-certainly on an annual basis, with on-site inspection likelihood rising to 50% after a suspicious transaction report (SAR) is filed, adverse media triggers enhanced supervision, or a custody wire routing anomaly is detected

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (NZ) — ss 12 (mode of incorporation), 13 (assent to incorporation), 15 (certificate of incorporation), 16 (company constitution), 199–201 (registered office and company records), s 172 (resident director requirement); supplemented by the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (Parts 5 and 6 for financial advice and discretionary investment management licences), and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 for the Multi-Family Office's licensed financial activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, MBIE); online portal: https://app.companiesoffice.govt.nz/co-app/
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: NZ Companies Office Form 3 – Incorporation Application, filed electronically via the Companies Office Register, together with the Company Constitution (Annexure A), consent-to-act forms, Registered Office declaration, and the digitally-issued Certificate of Incorporation; a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) is issued automatically upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Companies Act 1993 prescribes no minimum paid-up capital or escrow account; the International Company may be capitalised with zero or nominal issued shares. However, to obtain the FMA Financial Advice Provider (FAP) / Discretionary Investment Management Service (DIMS) licence, the applicant must demonstrate a minimum financial capacity of the New Zealand dollar equivalent of approximately USD 18,500 (NZD 30,000) available on standby, evidenced by a bank letter, to sustain continuity of client portfolio advisory operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [INTERNATIONAL COMPANY (MFO) LIMITED], held on [date] at the registered office, [registered office address], New Zealand.

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL
RESOLVED that the subscriber shareholdings set forth in the Incorporation Application be and they are hereby accepted, and that the initial ordinary shares, being 1,000 shares of NZD 1.00 each, be and are hereby allotted fully paid to the founding multi-family client trust vehicles as recorded in the Company's Share Register.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE
RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby confirmed at [street address, city, New Zealand] in accordance with section 199 of the Companies Act 1993, and that the Company's records, including the share register, board minutes, and accounting records, be physically maintained at that office.

3. GOVERNANCE AND OFFICER APPOINTMENTS
RESOLVED that, subject to the New Zealand director residency requirement and fit-and-proper standards, the following persons are hereby appointed with immediate effect: (a) Executive Director – [Name]; (b) Independent Non-Executive Director – [Name]; (c) Company Secretary – [Name]; and (d) AML/CFT Compliance Officer – [Name].

4. AUTHORISATION OF LICENSING AND REGULATORY ACTIONS
RESOLVED that the Compliance Director be and is hereby authorised to prepare and submit on behalf of the Company: (i) the application for registration on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR); (ii) the application to the Financial Markets Authority for a Financial Advice Provider licence and, where the Company exercises discretion over client portfolios, a Discretionary Investment Management Service licence; (iii) the AML/CFT risk assessment and compliance programme; and (iv) membership in an approved dispute resolution scheme (FSCL or BDRC).

CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Incorporation with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office New Zealand — digital Register at https://app.companiesoffice.govt.nz/co-app/
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Authenticate with RealMe, select 'Register a Company', enter the proposed corporate name and suffix 'Limited', and file Form 3 online. Attach the Company Constitution, consent to appointment of each director (Form 4), consent of each shareholder (Form 5), and declare the physical registered office and electronic address for service. All foreign directors and shareholders must verify identity via RealMe verification or attached certified passport copies, and at least one director must satisfy the New Zealand residency requirement under section 172 of the Companies Act 1993. Watch for automated registry checks; upon approval the electronically signed Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN are issued in one transaction.
required_dossiers: Form 3 - Incorporation Application (online)
Company Constitution (Annexure A) executed by subscribers
Form 4 - Consent to Appointment as Director
Form 5 - Consent to Act as Shareholder
Certified copy of passport / National ID for each director and shareholder (or RealMe verified identity)
Registered Office declaration with physical street address in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries or rejects the application, correct the listed defect (e.g., non-distinctive company name or unverified identity) within the correction window and re-submit using the same application reference. For an adverse name decision, request the Registrar to re-review within 20 working days under sections 22-23 of the Companies Act 1993, and if the refusal is maintained, apply for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration on the Financial Service Providers Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) / Registrar of Financial Service Providers — FSPR portal (https://www.fsp-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before application, obtain membership in an FMA-approved dispute resolution scheme (Financial Services Complaints Limited FSCL or Banking & Financial Services Ombudsman BDRC). Submit the online FSP application setting out the types of FMC Act services (financial advice, discretionary investment management, financial transaction services), nominate the AML/CFT compliance officer for each financial activity class, and pay the statutory registration fee. The registration is subject to annual confirmation and must be completed prior to requesting the substantive FMA licensing.
required_dossiers: FSPR application form with NZBN
Certificate of Incorporation (copy)
Dispute Resolution Scheme membership certificate (FSCL or BDRC)
Copy of first board resolution authorising the application
AML/CFT compliance officer nomination details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is suspended or queried, file the updated disclosure within 10 working days or resolve the inconsistency under section 20 of the Financial Service Providers Act 2008. An affected applicant may appeal the Registrar's final decision to the District Court within 20 working days. Ensure the annual confirmation is renewed to avoid removal of the FSP number, which would undermine the FMA licence application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: FMA Financial Advice Provider (FAP) and Discretionary Investment Management Service (DIMS) Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) of New Zealand — licensing department, using the FMA regulatory portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Under Part 5 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, the Multi-Family Office must hold a Financial Advice Provider licence for individual family-client portfolio advice; under Part 6 of the same Act, a DIMS licence is mandatory where the entity exercises a discretion to buy or sell financial products on behalf of its advisory clients. Draft and submit a comprehensive licensing pack detailing the corporate structure, fit-and-proper declarations for all directors and senior managers, the conflicts-of-interest and disclosure policy, client money and asset handling arrangements (custody rails: SWIFT interbank and custody wire), outsourcing register, business continuity plan, and evidence of financial capacity (bank letter confirming NZD 30,000 minimum standby). FMA statutory decision period is 90 working days from receipt of a materially complete application; an incomplete application may be declined without substantive review.
required_dossiers: FMA FAP Licence application under s 391 FMC Act 2013
DIMS Licence application under Part 6 FMC Act 2013 (where applicable)
Business plan and resourcing plan (staff, systems, capital)
Fit-and-proper assessment declarations for each director, officer and key shareholder
Conflicts-of-interest register and disclosure policy
Client Money and Asset Handling arrangement documentation
Financial capacity evidence — stand-by letter / bank solvency certificate
AML/CFT risk assessment and compliance programme
Dispute resolution scheme membership certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where FMA issues a 'notice of intention to decline' or an information deficiency letter, respond in writing within 10 working days and request a formal pre-decision conference. The applicant may amend the licensing pack and submit a revised compliance framework. If licence refusal is maintained, the applicant may seek the FMA's reasons under the Official Information Act 1982, then challenge the substantive decision by judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand within 28 days of the notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration and Compliance Programme Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) — acting as supervisor under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 28 days of obtaining the FAP/DIMS licence, the Multi-Family Office must register as an AML/CFT reporting entity with the FMA and confirm its nominated compliance officer on the FSPR. The board must formally approve the written AML/CFT risk assessment and the compliance programme, including customer due diligence (CDD) and enhanced CDD for 'high-risk' private-client structures, ongoing transaction monitoring for SWIFT and custody-wire rails, sanction screening, politically exposed person (PEP) identification and annual staff training. The approved programme must be filed with the supervisor and applied from the date of first client on-boarding.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT risk assessment approved by board
AML/CFT compliance programme (KYC/CDD/EDDD, monitoring, reporting)
Nomination of AML/CFT Compliance Officer with supporting CV/Fit and Proper
Annual AML/CFT training register for employees
Sanctions and PEP screening solution evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FMA issues a formal warning letter or a remedial direction, submit within 20 working days a corrective action plan covering the identified deficiencies, update the risk assessment and programme, and provide proof of implementation. In case of an infringement notice or other enforcement action, the reporting entity may make written submissions to the FMA and, where prescribed, seek judicial review of the decision. Voluntary self-disclosure of minor breaches before a warning letter is generally treated as mitigating.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety and Civil Defence Clearance (Evacuation Scheme & Building Warrant of Fitness)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) and the applicable territorial authority (local city/district council) under the Building Act 2004
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the physical advisory office, arrange a building inspection with the territorial authority and obtain a Compliance Schedule and annual Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) for the premises. Apply to FENZ for approval of an Evacuation Scheme (Form FENZ 301) if the workplace regularly has more than 18 persons present; the approved scheme must be rehearsed every six months with log books. Ensure the premises are structurally safe under the earthquake-prone building regime, and install and maintain fire alarm, emergency lighting, smoke control and means-of-escape systems per AS/NZS standards. Civil defence readiness includes a business continuity plan with 48-hour utility relocation for regulated client money operations.
required_dossiers: Application for Evacuation Scheme Approval (FENZ Form 301)
Compliance Schedule and annual BWOF issued by territorial authority
Fire alarm/egress installation certificates (Type 1/2 systems)
Six-monthly evacuation drill log
Earthquake-prone building assessment certificate (if required by district plan)
Business Continuity / Civil Defence readiness plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FENZ issues a non-compliance notice or improvement direction, cause the defect to be remedied by a certified contractor and request re-inspection within the directed deadline (generally 10 working days). If the territorial authority cancels the BWOF, immediately prepare a remedial Form 12 update and obtain a new building surveyor statement before the next MFO client-access working day. An unsafe premises notice under the Building Act 2004 may be appealed to the Building (Territorial Authority) complaints adjudication and ultimately the District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational Health and Safety Registration and WorkSafe Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment) under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the entity on the WorkSafe notification system ('PCBU notification') for the financial-advisory premises if the company has workers or engages contractors. Undertake the mandatory hazard identification, risk assessment and control methodology for the office environment; document the emergency response plan, first aid equipment provision, electrical safety checks (per Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010) and workstation ergonomics. Appoint a Health and Safety Officer and schedule an induction for all family-office employees and visiting client advisers. All notifiable incidents must be reported to WorkSafe immediately, and a complaint, risk, or negligence record must be maintained.
required_dossiers: WorkSafe NZ PCBU notification form
Health and Safety at Work policy and annual review record
Hazard register and risk assessments for office activities
First aid kit compliance and personnel certification list
Electrical equipment safety test record (Test and Tag Register)
Emergency and evacuation drill records (cross-referenced with FENZ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If WorkSafe issues an Improvement Notice or a Prohibition Notice, comply with the stated remedial steps within the specified period and provide written confirmation with photographic/engineering evidence; request a closure/clearance inspection once cured. A PCBU may challenge any notice by applying to the District Court within 28 days under section 224 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. Where a minor breach letter is issued, submit a corrective action plan within 10 working days to close the matter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) — for the principal financial-services licence; WorkSafe New Zealand and the territorial council — for physical workplace clearance; Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand and local regional council — for any incidental environmental requirements applicable to a professional office activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Advice Provider (FAP) Licence under Part 5 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Discretionary Investment Management Service (DIMS) Licence under Part 6 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (because the Multi-Family Office retains discretionary authority over client portfolios); plus Financial Service Providers Register number and AML/CFT Reporting Entity registration; for physical premises: Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) and FENZ Evacuation Scheme Approval.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, with the applicable regional council / territorial authority acting under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Permitted Activity — Exempt from a Full EIA. The Multi-Family Office operates exclusively in an indoor professional office environment with no industrial production, discharge point, or hazardous processes. Under the relevant district plan, office use for financial/administrative services is a permitted activity, and no resource consent or environmental impact assessment report is required. A trade-waste consent may be required only if the premises includes catering/discharge characteristics over the local by-law thresholds, and no such discharge is contemplated under the desk-based advisory model.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC or particulate emission limits apply to a financial advisory office, provided that all sanitary effluent discharges comply with the local council Water Services Trade Waste Bylaw (reference typical limits: pH 6–10, BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 250 mg/L in any trade-waste connection) and the National Environmental Standard for Sources of Human Drinking Water 2007 for any stormwater interactions. All office waste is to be minimised per the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; e-waste and fluorescent lamps must be handled by licensed contractors; HVAC refrigerants must comply with the Ozone Layer Protection Act 1996, and any emergency generator must meet diesel engine emission standards (EPA air quality NES) if installed solely for business continuity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017 (approved Evacuation Scheme, six-monthly drill log, annual fire systems inspection); Building Warrant of Fitness and annual compliance schedule under the Building Act 2004 (including escape routes, sprinkler/alarm panels, emergency lighting); structural/earthquake-prone building assessment where applicable; WorkSafe New Zealand health and safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (hazard register, first aid, incident reporting); electrical safety certificate under the Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010; and civil defence readiness in the form of a business continuity plan to protect client custody-wire and SWIFT banking rails during a natural disaster event.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; online self-service portal: myIR (accessed via www.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident International Company (IC) seeking a New Zealand tax identity must: (1) appoint a New Zealand-resident agent for service of notices; (2) complete Form IR742 (Application for an IRD Number for a Non-Resident Company) and file it with certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, and a register of directors and shareholders; (3) submit the application electronically through myIR or by post to Inland Revenue, PO Box 39050, Wellington Mail Centre 5045; (4) upon issuance of the IRD number (typically within 8–15 working days for paper and 1–2 working days for myIR), register separately for GST in myIR if NZD 60,000 or more of taxable supplies is made in any 12-month period, or voluntarily where zero-rating or input tax refunds will be claimed; (5) register for PAYE and FBT only if the IC employs personnel physically working in New Zealand. The IRD number operates as the single statutory tax identification number for income tax, GST, PAYE, FBT, and all other New Zealand taxes; there is no separate VAT registration number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no check-the-box regime. A non-resident International Company is taxed on a territorial basis: liability is limited exclusively to New Zealand-sourced income, while foreign-sourced income from offshore discretionary portfolio advisory and multi-family office activities remains outside the New Zealand tax net unless the company is managed and controlled in New Zealand or maintains a fixed establishment there. The company may elect: (a) GST grouping under sections 55–57 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 with New Zealand group members; (b) to be treated as a controlled foreign company shareholder if New Zealand residents hold 50% or more of the IC and their attributing interests trigger CFC income attribution; (c) to apply the NZ thin capitalisation and hybrid mismatch ordering rules under Part FM of the Income Tax Act 2007 and the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018, which disallow deductions for hybrid financial instrument payments and imported mismatched payments and override domestic treaty benefits where an offshore branch or hybrid entity is used.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — value-added tax levied under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold; non-resident suppliers of remote services (including digital and cross-border advisory services) to New Zealand consumers are also subject to the NZD 60,000 registration threshold under the GST (Remote Services) rules, with registration required once the threshold is exceeded unless the supplies are business-to-business and zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance regime, no API-based live invoice clearance, and no digital stamping or QR-code mandate exists in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the PEPPOL network (NZ e-Invoicing Service accredited by Inland Revenue). Tax invoices must contain the supplier's name and IRD number, date of issue, description of goods or services, GST-exclusive and GST-inclusive amounts, and the GST component, and must be issued within 28 days of the supply. GST returns are filed electronically via myIR under monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly filing cycles as allocated by Inland Revenue.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where: (a) goods are physically exported from New Zealand by the supplier within 28 days of the supply and the supplier holds contemporaneous evidence of export; (b) services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, provided the services are not physically performed in New Zealand and are not directly in connection with land in New Zealand or goods physically present in New Zealand at the time of supply; (c) for the multi-family office advisory model, discretionary portfolio advisory and asset-management services supplied to non-resident private client families will qualify for zero-rating where the services are provided for the purposes of a business or taxable activity carried on outside New Zealand and the recipient is not in New Zealand at the time the services are rendered. The supplier must retain a full audit trail evidencing the export, the non-resident status of the recipient, and the receipt of payment from offshore.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Electronic Export Declaration (Trade Single Window / AES export entry reference)
Commercial invoice and itemised advisory fee invoice describing the services or goods with HS codes and values
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of exported goods (for goods transactions)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of export consideration into a New Zealand bank account from the non-resident purchaser
Packing list, certificate of origin, and freight insurance certificate supporting the customs declared value
Signed client mandate or discretionary investment management agreement confirming non-resident status of the recipient and offshore place of benefit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may disallow zero-rating, claw back input tax credits, and assess output tax together with use-of-money interest for any GST shortfall. Civil shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply at graduated rates: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or intentional misleading conduct. Directors, shadow directors, and professional advisers involved in arranging a fraudulent export zero-rating scheme may incur personal liability as persons knowingly involved in the evasion. Criminal prosecution can result in imprisonment of up to 5 years, fines of up to NZD 50,000 for individuals and NZD 250,000 for companies, and forfeiture of goods under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 for false export declarations. Additionally, the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 imposes independent civil penalties for failure to maintain accurate wire-transfer and cross-border payment records for the custody and SWIFT payment rails used by the multi-family office.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ). New Zealand does not operate a separate foreign-exchange administration; the RBNZ is the consolidated monetary, prudential, and balance-of-payments statistical authority, while the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) of Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand administers the residual inbound foreign-investment screening regime under the Overseas Investment Act 2005.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand is an IMF Article VIII member: the New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible on both the current and the capital account, with no surrender, pledge, or repatriation restrictions. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and capital repayment from the New Zealand-operating multi-family office to the Cook Islands International Company are unrestricted, subject to (i) non-resident withholding tax at treaty-reduced rates and (ii) OIO screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for acquisitions of sensitive land, fishing quota, or significant business assets above statutory thresholds. The Cook Islands IC must preserve central management and control outside New Zealand in order to maintain non-residency for NZ tax purposes and to preserve the tax-exempt character of its income under Cook Islands law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no minimum conversion ratio, and no compulsory conversion timeline. Exporters and service providers may freely retain, convert, or deploy any foreign-currency receipts. Residual obligations are confined to (i) statistical reporting for the RBNZ balance-of-payments and international-investment-position surveys, (ii) border cash declarations under the AML/CFT Act 2009 for physical currency or bearer negotiable instruments equal to or exceeding NZD 10,000, and (iii) standard documentary substantiation required by the relevant NZ banking counterparty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Offshore-Director Operational Account
Operational, Trade Settlement, and FX Hedging Account
Capital Escrow Account and Transactional Operating Account
Multi-Family Office Private Banking and Custody-Wire Account
Domestic Operating Account (sub-optimal for offshore IC structures)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM (supplementary rail only; not a primary settlement layer). New Zealand has no bespoke electronic-money-institution licensing category. A cross-border digital EMI must (i) register on the Financial Service Providers Register, (ii) become a reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act 2009 in the money-remittance or foreign-exchange-dealer category, and (iii) avoid the deposit-taking prohibition under the Deposit Takers Act 2023. In practice, Wise Business and Airwallex-type providers can support low-value disbursements, but tier-1 NZ banks will not permit an EMI to serve as the settlement or escrow counterparty for a High_Risk_Special_License multi-family office; all rail-critical balances must reside in regulated NZ bank accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto mandate: face-to-face or equivalent live-video identity verification. Fully remote onboarding is not available for this profile. The bank must obtain direct knowledge of the directors and ultimate beneficial owners of both the Cook Islands IC and the NZ-operating MFO. The minimum standard comprises (i) an in-person or high-definition video interview with at least one director or UBO and the appointed NZ AML/CFT compliance officer; (ii) notarised and apostilled (or consular-legalised) corporate extracts, including registers of directors and shareholders; and (iii) a board resolution authorising account opening and enumerating signatories. ANZ, Westpac, and HSBC will accept the video interview where the onboarding package is certified by an NZ-licensed lawyer or licensed trustee company and the first inbound transfer originates from a pre-existing bank relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cook Islands-sourced corporate vehicle (perception of offshore secrecy and heightened scrutiny)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cook Islands International Company Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission; economic-substance evidence (Rarotonga registered office, in-country licensed trustee, board minutes held at the Cook Islands venue); CRS/AEOI self-certification; written opinion from NZ tax counsel confirming non-tax-residency in New Zealand; and three years of audited financial statements for the IC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unmapped beneficial-ownership chain of the underlying family trusts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trust deeds and a consolidated beneficial-ownership matrix showing each settlor, protector, and beneficiary class; certified extracts of the IC shareholder register; bank references from two incumbent tier-1 banks; and a copy of the NZ AML/CFT compliance programme filed with the designated supervisor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or concentrated high-net-worth source-of-wealth friction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent source-of-wealth report prepared in accordance with STEP (Society of Trust and Estate Practitioners) guidelines; audited family financial statements and notarised documentation of the original wealth-creating events (sale agreements, estate deeds, inheritances); and independent character and verification references from regulated counterparties in each family's home jurisdiction.

Current Financial Service Providers Register certificate; a Financial Advice Provider licence issued under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 where NZ-based advice or discretionary management is conducted; the AML/CFT fit-and-proper and compliance-officer appointments on file; and an engagement letter appointing a licensed statutory supervisor or trustee for custody assets.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Standard rail is a SWIFT MT103 from the Cook Islands IC's account to the NZ MFO's operational account at a tier-1 NZ bank. The payment must carry an ISO 20022 or MT103 purpose code mapping to the BPM6 classification: for a share-subscription contribution use 'EQUI' (equity capital); for an intragroup shareholder loan use 'LOAN'; for family settlement distributions use 'GIFT' or 'CLTR' (capital transfer) as appropriate. The receiving bank will require a board resolution, a certified register of the IC's directors and shareholders, a CRS/AEOI tax self-certification, an OIO approval letter where the funds will acquire sensitive NZ assets, and the NZ office's inward-remittance AML declaration. NZD proceeds settle through the RBNZ ESAS real-time gross settlement system; USD and EUR proceeds settle via SWIFT gpi through the NZ bank's correspondent network.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational and family disbursements are cleared by SWIFT MT103 messages (or MT104/MT105 consolidated batch instructions) with beneficiary BIC and IBAN validation and explicit remittance advice describing each payment purpose, e.g. 'trust distribution' or 'custody fee'. Trade settlement with commercial counterparties uses documentary collections and commercial letters of credit: the NZ bank issues the LC by SWIFT MT700, typically at sight or up to 90 days usance, with an overseas confirming bank where required. Domestic NZD liquidity is consolidated through the Payments NZ Bulk Electronic Clearing System and the ESAS high-value real-time gross settlement window, permitting same-day settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards in NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP and NZD/JPY, with tenors up to five years, transacted with a registered NZ bank counterparty
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies without a deliverable NZD market (e.g., CNY, INR, KRW) executed through onshore NZ banks, subject to RBNZ prudential and counterparty limits
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) used for long-dated hedging of trust investment liabilities, currency-matched distributions, and family-office liquidity
Vanilla FX options and FX swaps documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a supervised NZ bank or licensed foreign-bank branch

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s. 208) — statement of shareholding, directors, and registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Ministry of Business, Innovation & Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on the company's Return Date, being the anniversary of the incorporation date; online filing is open during the Return Date month plus a 20-working-day grace period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee NZ$61.46 (US$38); failure to file within 12 months of the Return Date is an offence and triggers a Registrar strike-off notice with administrative removal from the register; directors remain liable for continuing default penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Kōwhiti Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership (Companies (Disclosure of Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2023, ss. 95A–95V)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the Annual Return within 20 working days after the Return Date month; first confirmation applies to foreign-controlled and large companies from 13 December 2024, with subsequent annual confirmations on the incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Infringement notice up to NZ$10,500 (US$6,500) and criminal penalty up to NZ$50,000 (US$31,000) for false or omitted confirmation; repeated default supports strike-off action against the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: IR6 Company Income Tax Return (Income Tax Act 2007; Tax Administration Act 1994)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 7 July following a 31 March balance date where the company holds a tax-agent Notice of Extension; otherwise by 7 May. A Tax-Exempt-Zone International Company files a nil return claiming the statutory exemption.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZ$250 (US$155) plus NZ$50 (US$31) per additional 28-day period, capped at four periods; non-filing permits IRD default assessment under s. 141C and debt collection enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST-101 Goods and Services Tax Return (Goods and Services Tax Act 1985) — applicable if the multi-family office is GST-registered for management-fee income; offshore portfolio services may be zero-rated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due and payable by the 28th day following each taxable period; filing periods may be monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly, with the annual GST reconciliation aligned to the 31 March balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty plus 1% initial and 1.5% monthly incremental interest on unpaid GST; default assessment and forced collection under Part 11 of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: FBT Return (Fringe Benefit Tax Act 1985) — quarterly return for motor vehicles, low-interest loans, or other benefits provided to directors or employees of the MFO
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly, due by the 20th of the month following each quarter-end (30 June, 30 September, 31 December, 31 March); an annual filing option aligns with the 31 March tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 1% immediately plus 1.5% compounding monthly on net FBT; late filing attracts NZ$250 per instalment penalty plus accruing interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Report (s. 87, Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009) — including risk-assessment summary, compliance monitoring metrics, and suspicious-transaction statistics
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as AML/CFT supervisor for discretionary portfolio management service providers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 September covering the 1 July – 30 June reporting year; submission is made through the FMA online portal. No separate filing fee; annual AML/CFT supervisory levy is assessed under the AML/CFT Fees and Levies Regulations 2016.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: FMA formal warning, civil penalty up to NZ$1,000,000 (US$620,000) for a reporting entity, or criminal prosecution of the compliance officer; repeat failure may trigger licence suspension under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and DIMS Licence Compliance Return (Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, Part 6; Companies Act 1993, ss. 194–202)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for licensed DIMS providers; New Zealand Companies Office only where the entity meets 'large' reporting thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of balance date (generally by 30 September for a 31 March balance date); audited statements must be delivered to shareholders and filed on the FMA portal within the licence-conditions timeline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare and deliver financial statements is an offence under s. 202 of the Companies Act 1993; a DIMS-licensed MFO in breach faces FMA licence suspension, civil penalties, and adverse fit-and-proper findings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit applies under FMC Act 2013, s. 455–456 to any FMC reporting entity, which includes a DIMS-licensed multi-family office holding or controlling client money/money-related property; the 'large' company threshold (total assets above NZ$60m, revenue above NZ$30m, or 50+ full-time-equivalent employees) also triggers audit. Otherwise, shareholders holding 5% or more of the voting shares may demand an audit under Companies Act 1993, s. 199.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For-profit reporting entities must apply NZ IFRS (Tier 1 full) or NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2); non-reporting small companies may adopt the XRB NZ IFRS Simplified Framework Tier 3 (accrual) or Tier 4 (hybrid cash); a Tax-Exempt-Zone International Company that is not an FMC reporting entity may prepare special-purpose financial statements under XRB A1.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies (Disclosure of Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2023, every New Zealand company must maintain a confidential Kōwhiti register of beneficial owners and file an annual confirmation of beneficial ownership with the Companies Office alongside the Annual Return; any share transfer or change in significant control during the year must be recorded in the Kōwhiti register within 10 working days and is reflected in the next annual confirmation, without public disclosure to the open register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of general meetings and board resolutions (s. 189)
Kōwhiti Beneficial Ownership Register (Companies (Disclosure of Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2023)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200–US$2,500 per annum for New Zealand registered office, resident agent, corporate secretariat, and AML/CFT compliance officer services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$9,000–US$18,000 per annum for a certified CA ANZ audit firm reviewing consolidated multi-family office financial statements, scaled to assets under management and transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential corporate zones exist in New Zealand. The 28% headline rate is applied to the net assessable income of a company. Preferential treatment is available through (1) the R&D Tax Incentive refundable tax credit at 15% of eligible R&D expenditure; (2) the Australian/NZ imputation credit system for resident dividends, which eliminates double taxation; and (3) the indefinite carry-forward of tax losses subject to shareholder continuity requirements. Interest limitation rules and thin capitalisation may restrict debt deductions for foreign-controlled MFO structures.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite, subject to s IA 5 Income Tax Act 2007 shareholder continuity rules: losses are available only if minimum shareholder continuity of 49% is maintained and, for losses used after a continuity break between 49% and 66%, the company must continue to carry on the same business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return; non-resident companies file via Inland Revenue myIR/eFile using the IR4 return for a company with New Zealand-source taxable income and a completed IRD non-resident ownership schedule. Electronic filing through myIR Business or an approved tax agent software is mandatory for most companies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; companies with residual income tax above NZ$5,000 also pay provisional tax three times per year in addition to filing the annual IR4.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July if filed online or by 7 June if filed on paper. Terminal tax in respect of the income year is due by 7 February of the following year. A registered tax agent may obtain an extension to 31 March of the following year for filing, but payment deadlines remain enforceable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company IRD number, legal name, postal address, registered office, and contact email.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the New Zealand IRD number allocated to the non-resident company and state the country of tax residence. Attach the company's foreign registration number and list the principal foreign shareholder entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance date and tax year covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the New Zealand tax year corresponding to the company's balance date. A non-resident may use an approved substituted accounting period if the IRD has granted approval; otherwise the statutory 31 March balance date applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income, including business income, dividends, interest, royalties, and other income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income having a New Zealand source. Isolate New Zealand source management fees, performance fees, custody fees, and advisory income in a separate supporting schedule. Foreign source income is generally excluded unless the company is also tax-resident in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses claimed against assessable income, including salaries, rent, professional fees, software, depreciation, and interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate expenses on a just and reasonable basis to the New Zealand source income. Do not deduct expenses incurred to earn exempt foreign or offshore trust income. Transactions with associated offshore entities must reflect arm's-length amounts or transfer-pricing adjustments will be made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or net loss before loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company computes its net taxable income on its New Zealand business and investment income only. Losses arising from exempt foreign income cannot be offset against New Zealand source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward from previous years applied in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses that satisfy the 49% shareholder continuity test throughout the loss year and the current year may be claimed. For losses where continuity is between 49% and 66%, the same-business test must also be met. Attach a continuity schedule.

This is the figure to which the 28% company rate is applied. A non-resident company may not apply any foreign tax credit against New Zealand income tax unless a relevant DTA and foreign tax credit schedule is certified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable after imputation credits, RWT, foreign tax credits, and provisional tax payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company has paid NRWT to New Zealand on behalf of a non-resident shareholder, such withholding is a final tax on the shareholder, not a credit against the company's income tax. Include any New Zealand RWT credits on bank interest and verify DTA withholding rate claims using a certificate of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax or terminal tax payable, plus use-of-money interest calculation if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay residual tax by 7 February for a standard balance date. Non-resident companies with a non-resident tax agent may be eligible for different provisional tax timing; otherwise the same statutory payments are enforced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of cross-border related-party transactions, transfer-pricing method applied, and contemporaneous documentation position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors controlling the MFO must file an IRD International Transactions Disclosure form when the company has related-party dealings. Attach a Local File for controlled transactions above the applicable threshold and an OECD-compliant Master File if the investor group is in the Country-by-Country Reporting zone.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties apply under s 139B Tax Administration Act 1994: NZ$50 for each day or part-day that the return is late, capped at NZ$500 for each unfiled return. Late payment penalties and use-of-money interest accrue on any unpaid terminal tax from the statutory due date. Repeated refusal to file can trigger a 'failure to furnish return' offence with criminal fines and IRD debt collection actions, including statutory demand, liquidation, and director departure prohibition orders.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on gross dividends paid by a New Zealand resident company to a non-resident shareholder. For New Zealand resident shareholders, a 33% Resident Withholding Tax (RWT) may apply before imputation credits are set off. A dividend is subject to NZ company income tax first and then final NRWT at the statutory rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a Double Tax Agreement, the paying NZ company must receive a complete and timely certificate of tax residence (TRC) from the non-resident shareholder's foreign tax authority. The payee must also satisfy the DTA's limitation-of-benefits / purpose test, where present. The payer submits the TRC and a completed IRD Form IR290 declaration to Inland Revenue via myIR, and in practice the IRD endorses the entitlement before payment is made. The reduced DTA rate is applied only where the shareholder is the beneficial owner of the dividend, has not been interposed for treaty-shopping purposes, and the relevant treaty articles so provide. Retroactive claims are possible through an IRD claim and foreign tax credit adjustment process, but penalties can apply for incorrect claims.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT is 15% for both cross-border royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rates generally reduce these amounts: most NZ DTAs provide 10% for interest and 5% for royalties. An Australian or US resident may qualify for 0-15% interest or dividend rates depending on treaty type and shareholding thresholds. Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% of gross interest is available to an approved NZ issuer as an alternative to NRWT on certain interest payments to non-residents, provided the payer is an approved issuer and the lender is not associated with the payer.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A contemporaneous Local File is expected where the aggregate value of the taxpayer's cross-border controlled transactions exceeds NZ$1 million per taxpayer per income year, or earlier where the transaction involves a high-risk arrangement or the taxpayer is otherwise a large enterprise. A Master File is required for multinational groups whose consolidated annual revenue exceeds the Country-by-Country Reporting threshold of NZ$1.3 billion (equivalent to EUR 750 million). Lower thresholds can apply for high-risk intercompany services or intangible transactions and for transactions involving NZ loss-making or zero-taxed entities.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not administer a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but applies OECD BEPS-aligned rules and its general anti-avoidance rule (s BG1 Income Tax Act 2007) to disregard arrangements lacking genuine commercial substance. A multi-family office using an International Company must have demonstrable substance: physical office in New Zealand, resident directors, locally employed professional staff, board decision-making in New Zealand, and accounting records maintained in New Zealand. Failure to maintain such substance will cause the entity to be treated as tax resident where central management and control lies, and may result in denial of treaty benefits, anti-avoidance reconstruction, or re-attribution of the MFO's service income to a New Zealand agency or permanent establishment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False or Misleading Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting discretionary portfolio management fees, performance fees, or carried interest; fabricating invoices to foreign shell companies; suppressing books and records; or deliberately failing to report the existence of an offshore trust that controls the MFO's income stream.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax shortfall penalties: 20% for lack of reasonable care, 20% for unacceptable tax position, 100% for abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Criminal conviction under s 143 Tax Administration Act 1994: imprisonment up to 5 years and/or a fine of up to NZ$250,000 for a body corporate and NZ$50,000 for an individual. The IRD may also assess use-of-money interest and obtain an Anton Piller order for records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knew or ought to have known of the false position are jointly and severally liable for the company's statutory shortfall penalties where they materially contributed to the return. Civil restitution may be ordered, and IRD can apply for a departure prohibition order preventing the director from leaving New Zealand. Reckless trading under s 135 Companies Act 1993 exposes directors to personal liability for company debts, including unpaid tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging artificially high management fees from a related offshore entity to the New Zealand MFO; financing the MFO with non-arm's-length interest-free shareholder loans; embedding disproportionate profit in a low-tax foreign affiliate; filing no transfer-pricing documentation when controlled transactions exceed the threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD will recompute taxable income under the arm's-length principle using the most appropriate OECD method. Shortfall penalties apply: 20% for failing to take reasonable care, 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for intentional understatement. Interest is applied from the original due date until full payment. Cross-border financing can also be denied under thin capitalisation rules and the interest limitation rule for large MNE groups.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or implement a manipulative transfer-pricing policy may be subject to the same civil penalties as significant participants. The company veil may be pierced if the offshore entity is a mere instrumentality and the director caused the company to enter into sham transactions. Personal travel notifications and departure prohibitions may be issued in respect of unpaid tax liabilities of the controlled company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance / General Anti-Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a New Zealand-incorporated International Company exclusively as a mailbox entity, maintaining no employees, having no NZ business premises, holding board meetings outside New Zealand, and routing all discretionary family-office advisory decisions through an offshore trust while the commercial substance sits with the New Zealand MFO.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reconstruction under s BG1 and Part G Income Tax Act 2007: IRD may void the arrangement and attribute the income to the entity with actual economic substance; the shell company may be treated as resident in New Zealand based on central management and control; DTA benefits may be denied for lack of beneficial ownership or economic substance; shortfall penalties up to 100% and criminal penalties for evasion may apply if the arrangement is fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for the company's tax shortfall under s 141 TAA if they knowingly participated in the tax avoidance arrangement. The court may lift the corporate veil and impose civil restitution against directors in their personal capacities. Directors may also be disqualified from acting as directors under s 383 Companies Act 1993 and may face travel bans through IRD enforcement measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Breach and Unlicensed Financial-Service Provision
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a multi-family office with discretionary investment authority without holding the required Financial Advice Provider licence or being registered as a financial service provider under the FSP Act 2008; failing to undertake customer due diligence and beneficial-ownership verification before effecting swift-wire or custody transfers; failing to report suspicious transactions connected to offshore trusts or shell companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, a reporting entity can face substantial civil penalties of up to NZ$5 million for serious non-compliance, with individual penalties up to NZ$500,000; knowingly making false or misleading AML/CFT information is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment up to 2 years. The Financial Markets Authority may suspend, impose conditions on, or cancel the licence. Under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, providing unlicensed financial advice may attract fines up to NZ$1 million per breach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are presumed to be responsible for ensuring the AML/CFT compliance programme is adequate. Individuals who knowingly direct or approve a breach may be personally prosecuted and barred from managing financial service companies. Courts can order compensation and civil restitution to investors. Travel bans may be imposed for unpaid penalties or in aid of enforcement of personal liability orders.
